We have seen this mantra challenged on two fronts by both Russia and China of late. And so I wanted to start with China, particularly since you just got back from your third trip in the region and you just started a forced posture review that will ultimately shift resources from other theaters and send them west. And as you know, some of your predecessors also tried to do this shift west, but ultimately there were too many competing priorities in the Middle East, and that shift didn't really happen. background.speaker: [target]
background.text: First, I'd like to point out, Tara, that a new administration coming in, one of the first things that you'd expect for us to do is take inventory of where all of our capabilities or all of our forces are, and we want to make sure that our footprint matches our priorities. But it's not just forces, it's capability.

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: And I think we have to remember that we have capability in all warfighting domains, air, land, sea, and also space and cyber, and undersea capability as well.
